newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian Lever expects better second half 1996.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian Lever expects better second half 1996.

text.p: Nigerian conglomerate Lever Brothers on Tuesday said it expected profits to rise in the second half of 1996 after first half profits dropped against the same period of 1995.

"Performance in the second quarter of 1996 was better than the first quarter due to cost effective innovations in the form of new product introductions and an improved business mix. This improvement is expected to be sustained during the second half of 1996," said chief executive officer Rufus Giwa in a statement.
After tax profit fell to 636 million naira from 747 million naira in 1995.
Turnover rose to 4,244 million naira from 3,741 million naira, but pre-tax profit fell to 876.6 million naira from 1,183 million naira in 1995.
"The result reflects the company's decision to accept lower profit margins in view of the depressed consumer purchasing power," Giwa said.
Shares first fell three kobo to 25.60 naira in Tuesday trading, but recovered to close at 25.65 naira up two kobo on the day.
Some traders said confidence remained in the company despite the lower than anticipated result. But others were bearish and said there was no sign of an increase in consumer spending.
Anglo-Dutch Unilever owns a total of 38.21 percent of shares. Total overseas investment in the company is 50.04 percent.
